text:
maya: Heads-up, I ran a long nsys capture for the 32->64 batch/shard threshold regression we saw in canary today. timeline looks weird, posting top findings.
ravi: nice, paste the rough timeline snippet and the command you used so I can reproduce.
maya: command: `nsys profile --output=run_kv_32to64 --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=none ./bench --model=redwood-small --batch=dynamic`\nI trimmed to the heavy shot (first 2s after request). main observations: kernel selection flips at batch 48 -> we fall back to a different matmul kernel with much higher L2 traffic.
jonathan: when you say "flip" do you mean we intentionally choose an alternate kernel or an unintended codepath? any perf counters?
maya: looks like unintended. nvcc kernel name map: `mm_dense_fp16_tile32` vs `mm_dense_fp16_tile64_fallback`. the fallback has ~2.6x more DRAM read bytes in Nsight counters. snippet from nsys report:\n```\nTime (ms)  Stream  API/Activity                     Kernel Name                      DRAM Read (MB)\n12.34      s0      Kernel                            mm_dense_fp16_tile32             12.1\n12.89      s0      Kernel                            mm_dense_fp16_tile64_fallback    32.6\n13.45      s1      memcpy H2D                        cudaMemcpyAsync                  6.4\n```\nravi: interesting — that fallback could explain latency spike. where does the memcpy fit? is it blocking the faster kernel stream?
maya: that's the odd part: Nsight waterfall shows memcpy on stream 1 overlapping with kernel on stream 0, but there's a 300us CPU thread gap before we enqueue the fast kernel. timeline: memcpy starts at 13.4ms on s1, kernel ready on s0 at 13.35ms but actual launch is 13.65ms. looks like host thread was paused. attaching my annotated perfetto link: https://perfetto.link/trace/abcd123 (internal)
jonathan: could be scheduler preemption on the prefetch/dispatcher thread. any linux perf lost-samples? what user threads are tied to those cuda launches?
maya: yes — perf record shows the dispatcher thread (redwood-batcher:prefetch) had a 0.26ms scheduling gap right before the enqueue call. `ps -eo pid,comm,pri,ni | grep redwood` showed normal prio, but we had cpu steal during that interval on the node. also saw kvcache eviction churn around the same time — eviction thread woke and did a ~1.8ms spike of memcpy+hash work.
perf-bot: Auto-detected correlation: high host CPU contention (3 events) + nvtx markers show PREFETCH_START at 13.1ms and KVCACHE_EVICT at 13.3ms. Possible priority inversion.
ravi: can we repro by forcing the batcher dispatcher onto a dedicated CPU (taskset) or increasing thread priority?
maya: tried `taskset -c 6 ./bench` and pinning dispatcher with `pthread_setschedparam(SCHED_FIFO, 45)` temporarily — the launch gap disappears and nsight shows consistent mm_dense_fp16_tile32 selection. latency median drops ~18% in that run.
jonathan: good signal. but why does kernel selector choose fallback when delayed? is it a timing-dependent heuristic (sequence length / padding) or based on TKERNEL heuristics sampling runtime shapes?
maya: digging into selector logs, it's based on an optimistic path that assumes sufficient queued tokens for tile32; when CPU enqueue is delayed past a 200us threshold we degrade to tile64 to avoid bank conflicts observed in microbenchmarks. That threshold seems too brittle under host jitter.
ravi: two mitigation ideas: 1) move selector decision closer to kernel launch time (re-evaluate after prefix prefetch completes), 2) make fallback less aggressive (raise threshold) so we don't switch for short transient host pauses.
jonathan: agree. also consider raising priority for enqueue thread in Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbors causing regression. for Private/VPC maybe document a recommended cpu-affinity.
maya: I'll open a small PR: (a) add an additional pre-launch check to re-evaluate kernel choice if host enqueue delayed >100us, (b) expose `selector_host_time_threshold_us` as a config with default 250->1000 us for Dedicated. will also add nvtx annotations around the selector to aid future traces.
perf-bot: queued issue PERF-1229: "Kernel selector flips under host enqueue jitter -> fallback to tile64" with reproducer link.
sre-bot: FYI, node we used had recent kernel updates; filing infra ticket to repro across node pools. tagging oncall.
ravi: thanks maya — can you attach the full nsys .qdrep to the ticket and include the small annotated perf record? I'll try repro on an older kernel and a newer one.
maya: uploaded qdrep to PERF-1229 and linked the perf.data. short-term: deploy PR with selector re-check behind a feature flag so we can A/B test on canary.
jonathan: :thumbsup: also add telemetry event when selector flips with surrounding host gap so we can measure how often this happens in prod.
maya: will do. closing loop after canary runs tomorrow. thanks all.
